title: Sales Engineer Dry-run Cards + Scripts (WIP)
body:
Purpose and context:
- Quick, lightweight slide+card set for SE dry-runs before pilot kickoff. Focus: fast technical credibility, clear fallback paths, and a 5-minute latency/cost triage for trial runs.
- Audience: Sales Engineers (frontline), Solutions Engineers, AE technical champions.
- Goal: reduce time-to-first-success on pilots, prevent common fail modes during live demo or initial integration.

How to use this file (ops notes):
- Use the cards as speaker prompts during a 20–30 minute dry-run with the AE.
- Run through the checklist, then role-play 2 objections: "latency spikes" and "cost looks high on our budget."
- Capture any missed items in the pilot template (linked in linked_artifacts).

Slide 1: Opening frame (30s)
- Title: Pilot Kickoff — What success looks like in 30 days
- Speak to outcomes, not features: "<X> user journeys instrumented, <Y> latency below SLA, regression guardrails in place."
- One-liner on deployment choice: Hosted (fastest), Dedicated (predictable throughput), Private (data controls).

Slide 2: Quick architecture + routing cues (1.5 min)
- Visual: client -> Redwood API -> model routing policy (primary: redwood/gpt-3.5-opt, fallback: redwood/gpt-3.5-quant)
- Talk track bullets: region affinity, reserve vs burst capacity, circuit-breaker fallback to lower-cost variant under high queue depth.

Slide 3: 5-minute latency & cost triage (demo checklist)
- Quick checks to run at dry-run:
  - Are requests streaming? If yes, does the UI start rendering before end-token? (helps perceived latency)
  - Check median/95th token latency in Console (demo) & local curl timings.
  - Confirm batching config: default, per-route override? Large batch sizes hurt p95 on small interactive flows.
- Example commands (copy-ready):
  - curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d '{"model":"<model>","prompt":"ping\n"}' | jq
  - Note: For latency demos, use sequence length = 64 and turn off large context to compare apples-to-apples.

Slide 4: Fallback mapping (quick chart)
- Primary model: redwood/serene-16b (latency: 150–250ms, cost: $$$)
- Cheap fast fallback: redwood/compact-3b-Int8 (latency: 80–120ms, cost: $)
- Graceful downgrade rules: if queue depth > 30 requests per GPU or single-request p95 > SLA, route to fallback; for hallucination regression, route to reranker + conservative prompt template.
- Speak track: "We never fully call the lower-cost model in canary — we shadow first, then flip with A/B and rollback hooks in Console."

Slide 5: Objection playcards (scripts + counters)
- Objection: "Latency is too variable."
  - SE script: "I hear you — can we step through the Console p95 trace and your traffic pattern? Typical fixes are batching tuning, streaming, or switching to a lower-latency instance family. We can run an A/B for 24h to show difference."
- Objection: "Cost is unpredictable / spikes."
  - SE script: "We’ll enable token-level cost breakdown, set hard caps and route heavy workloads to cached pipelines or cheaper quantized variants. Also run an Optimize report to suggest a quantization profile."
- Objection: "We need on-prem visibility / audit logs."
  - SE script: "Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM and audit stream; we’ll scope a minimal VPC config for the pilot and verify log export in week 1."

Slide 6: Rapid role-play (5min)
- SE plays AE; AE plays platform architect. Run both objections above plus a surprise: "What if our prompt mix includes many long contexts?"
- Expected SE actions: explain token cost scaling, suggest prefix caching, propose pre-tokenization and KV-cache warm strategies.

Slide 7: Canary & rollback checklist (single page)
- Canary: 5–10% traffic -> run for 24–72h; monitor p95, cost/unit, correctness on golden set.
- Rollback triggers: correctness regression > 3% on eval set, p95 > SLA for two consecutive 1h windows, error rate > 1%.
- Rollforward plan: increase to 25% -> 50% -> 100% with 2x monitoring cadence.

Slide 8: Quick win scripts for demos (copy-paste)
- Basic latency sanity: curl + timestamps, sample payload with 64 tokens
- Shadow run pattern: POST to /v1/generate with header X-Shadow: true to test fallback without impacting live flows
- Billing check: call Console API for usage export (demo only)

Slide 9: Pre-flight checklist (before pilot start)
- Credentials: AE + SE + customer dev have API keys? (yes/no)
- Telemetry: Console access for customer? Exposure level set?
- Load profile: expected qps, payload size distribution (p50/p95), peak hours specified?
- Escalation matrix: who to call for a critical fallback (names + rotation) — placeholder entries included.

Slide 10: Known open questions (notes-to-self)
- Do we have a sample A/B dashboard template for canary? (action: Diego to check Confluence page X)
- Can Solutions Engineering pre-seed a small dataset for golden correctness checks? (action: Priya to follow up)
- Should we include a "cost forecast" slide that runs projected monthly spend at expected qps? (include in next rev)

Appendix: quick heuristics & one-liners for SEs
- "If p95 > 2x median, look for batching or tail queuing — adjust max batch latency to lower p95 at cost of throughput."
- "Streaming reduces perceived latency even when token-level wall time remains similar."
- "Shadow first, flip later — observable rollback beats optimistic flips every time."

TODOs and next edits:
- Convert these cards into printable 3x5 cards for booth use (Sara)
- Record a 6-min demo video walking the triage steps (Tom)
- Add a slide showing 'billing at a glance' with concrete numbers for small/medium/large pilots (Amina)

Freeform notes (raw):
- Keep language simple — customers hate model names that sound like wizardry. Use categories: high-fidelity / balanced / low-cost.
- Consider adding a micro-deck for data-sensitive customers that focuses only on Private deployment checklist and KMS flows.
- Example anecdote to include in final: "Customer X reduced P95 by 40% after switching to compact-3b-Int8 for chat UI and enabling prefix caching — saved 62% monthly inference spend. (need anonymized permission)"

Contact / owner: Amina Patel — ping in slack @amina for questions or to schedule the dry-run.

Status: draft — ready for internal SE dry-run next Tuesday.
